It Takes Two is one of those games that managed to make me appreciate genres I normally wouldn’t enjoy. Its level design is exceptionally well-crafted, with seven completely different chapters, each offering its own unique gameplay ideas and atmosphere. What makes it even better is how well the story complements these changes, making every chapter feel meaningful rather than simply different for the sake of variety.

For me, the third chapter was the highlight of the game. The variety and creativity in its level design are incredible, constantly introducing new ideas and mechanics. The ending of the chapter was also one of the funniest moments I’ve ever had in a co-op game. My friend and I were laughing so hard that we literally couldn’t even control our characters anymore.

Overall, It Takes Two delivers an excellent co-op experience. My main criticism is that the puzzles and platforming are too easy. They rarely require you to really think or engage with the mechanics, which often made me breeze through the levels without much effort.

Even with that criticism, the creativity, variety, and sheer fun of the experience make it an absolute 10/10 for me.

It Takes Two é um jogo muito divertido e criativo, que se destaca principalmente pela necessidade de cooperação entre os jogadores. A história é emocionante e mostra a importância do diálogo, da união e do trabalho em equipe. Além disso, o jogo apresenta cenários variados, desafios criativos e uma jogabilidade dinâmica, fazendo com que cada momento seja diferente e envolvente. É uma ótima experiência para jogar com outra pessoa, proporcionando diversão e também uma reflexão sobre relacionamentos e parceria.

Am guessing I'm anywhere from halfway to three fourths done with the storyline by now.  Plays well-enough in splitscreen from a docked Steam Deck, was glad I stayed mostly spoiler-free before starting the story, and am pleased with how well the overall design of almost all of it has lived up to the hype.

If I had to name a weakest-link point in the game, the only that I can recall as of typing this would be a boating segment where each main character is paddling their respective side of a ship either forwards or backwards.  It's not bad, and it's not annoyingly long, either,  It just doesn't make for as interesting or varied a range of coordination types necessary, or puzzles to solve, or actions to be done to defeat opponents, compared to other standout well-designed sections.

This game's actually really cool. I went into this expecting it to be a puzzle solving cozy game with a bit of action to it fit for couples but it's so much more then that. There's fun minigames to get competitive with, loads of tracebacks to nostalgia, creative combat and uses of certain tools for each area, this game really did it's best of pushing the limits of what you could do with everyday house tools.

I think my favorite part about this game is the mix to different genre types, like for one area you'll be playing a dunegon game, then into a adventure, atmospheric type game, straight to a hogwarts fantasy. It feels so refreshing to be able to experience all sorts of game types without actually needing the knowledge to play them, I love it's balance.

Also can confirm, this game leads to divorce. I'm luvin' it!
